title: Reticle Inspection - CD Variation Detection on WaferSight PWG
subtitle: Post-Etch Quality Validation for 28nm Node Manufacturing
author: Maria Gonzalez

sections.1_OBJECTIVE:
This test case validates the capability of the WaferSight PWG system to detect and classify CD Variation defects during post-etch inspection at the 28nm technology node. The test is conducted at Pyeongtaek Fab 2 to ensure manufacturing quality standards are met for 200mm wafer production.

The primary objective is to verify that the inspection system meets the required detection sensitivity and classification accuracy for CD Variation defects that are critical to yield at the 28nm node. This test case is part of the ongoing qualification program for the WaferSight PWG platform.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Product Line: WaferSight PWG
- Inspection Type: Reticle Inspection
- Target Defect: CD Variation
- Process Step: Post-Etch
- Wafer Size: 200mm
- Technology Node: 28nm
- Fab Location: Pyeongtaek Fab 2

This test case applies to all WaferSight PWG systems deployed at Pyeongtaek Fab 2 for post-etch monitoring in the 28nm manufacturing line. Results from this test are used to establish baseline performance metrics and to qualify new recipe configurations.
sections.3_TEST_CONFIGURATION:
System: WaferSight PWG
Software Version: v8.4.866
Recipe: RETICLE_INSPECTION_28nm_POST_ETCH
Illumination Mode: Brightfield
Scan Speed: Medium (104 mm/s)
Pixel Size: 0.5μm
Edge Exclusion: 2mm
Sampling Plan: 5-point sampling
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Power on the WaferSight PWG system and allow 30-minute warm-up period.
2. Load the calibration wafer and run the standard calibration routine.
3. Verify calibration results are within specification (±2% tolerance).
4. Load the test wafer onto the stage using the automated handler.
5. Select the 'Reticle Inspection' recipe from the recipe library.
6. Configure detection sensitivity to target CD Variation defects.
7. Set scan parameters: full wafer scan with edge exclusion of 3mm.
8. Initiate the inspection run and monitor real-time defect map.
9. Upon completion, review the defect density map and classification results.
10. Export results to the factory automation system (SECS/GEM interface).
11. Compare results against the golden reference baseline.
12. Document any anomalies and generate the summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Defect detection sensitivity must meet 28nm node requirements
- False positive rate shall not exceed 5% of total detected events
- Scan throughput must be ≥ 72 wafers per hour
- Classification accuracy shall be ≥ 92% for known defect types
- Repeatability (3-sigma) shall be within ±0.9% for Reticle Inspection
- System uptime during test shall be ≥ 98%
- All results must be traceable through the MES integration
- Measurement correlation with reference tool shall be ≥ 0.94 R²
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Test Execution Date: 2025-03-06
Wafers Tested: 14
Total Defects Found: 4049
Defect Density: 1288.84 defects/cm²
Nuisance Rate: 3.6%
Capture Rate: 90.8%
Test Duration: 377 minutes
System Uptime: 97.7%

Result Classification: CONDITIONAL PASS
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The WaferSight PWG demonstrated acceptable performance in detecting CD Variation at the 28nm node.

b) The capture rate exceeded the minimum threshold, confirming system readiness.

c) Nuisance rate is within acceptable limits.

d) Cross-correlation with the reference SEM confirmed classification accuracy.

e) Recipe portability between systems at this fab was confirmed.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
The following corrective actions are recommended:

1. Review edge-zone detection parameters for optimization.
2. Schedule follow-up test after recipe optimization.
3. Monitor performance over next 30 production days.
